say: Scientists ask a narrow question: is this food, from this event, as safe as the conventional food it replaces? Assessors check whether the new protein could be toxic, and whether it could cause an allergy.

panel.heading: Six things WHO says are assessed

say: They measure key nutrients and natural toxins, and check that the inserted gene stays stable over generations.

panel.heading: Six things WHO says are assessed

say: And they look for nutritional effects, and for any change nobody planned. Eating DNA is not a risk in itself. Digestion breaks it down.

panel.heading: Six things WHO says are assessed

say: The GM plant is grown beside a conventional comparator. In a practice example, a GM cowpea has 24.1 grams of protein per 100 grams, and the comparator 23.5.

panel.heading: Reading a side-by-side comparison
items: GM line: 24.1 g protein per 100 g

say: The difference is 0.6 grams, about 2.6 percent.

panel.heading: Reading a side-by-side comparison
items: GM line: 24.1 g protein per 100 g

say: Ordinary varieties range from 20.0 to 28.0 grams, so this is normal. But if a natural anti-nutrient were 40 percent higher and outside the range, it would need explanation before approval.

panel.heading: Reading a side-by-side comparison
items: GM line: 24.1 g protein per 100 g
panel.rule: Worry about differences that are large or outside the normal range.

say: WHO states that GM foods on the international market have passed safety assessments and are not likely to present risks for human health.

panel.heading: What WHO does and does not say
left: Not likely to present health risks
Assess each food case by case
right: Every GM food is automatically safe
GM foods are proven to cause disease
Labelling rules are the same everywhere

say: Read it carefully. It covers foods that passed assessment. It does not say every possible GM food is safe. That is exactly why regulation exists.

say: Insects evolve. If Bt plants kill almost every pod borer, rare resistant survivors mate and the trait wears out. A refuge of non-Bt plants nearby keeps the population susceptible.
For example, Ngozi farms 2 hectares in Benue.

panel.heading: A refuge slows resistance
items: Strip along a 100 m side: 40 m deep

say: Suppose her leaflet says 20 percent refuge. That is 4,000 square metres.

panel.heading: A refuge slows resistance
items: Strip along a 100 m side: 40 m deep

say: She plants 16,000 square metres of Bt cowpea, and a strip 40 metres deep of non-Bt cowpea. One farmer who skips the refuge weakens the trait for every neighbour.

panel.heading: A refuge slows resistance
items: Strip along a 100 m side: 40 m deep
panel.rule: Use the refuge size in your own seed's stewardship guide.

say: Economic claims cut both ways. Here is an illustrative table. The prices are for practice only.

card.title: Seed plus spray cost for 1 hectare

say: Conventional seed costs about 30,000 naira, and 6 sprays for pod borer about 72,000. That is 102,000 naira.

card.title: Seed plus spray cost for 1 hectare

say: Bt seed costs more, about 45,000 naira, but needs only 2 sprays, 24,000. That is 69,000 naira, a difference of 33,000.
But if pest pressure is low and you only spray twice anyway, conventional seed is cheaper. Use your own records.

say: GM or not, everyday hazards remain. Dry grain well, because mould and aflatoxin grow in damp maize and groundnuts.

cards.d: Mould and aflatoxin grow in badly dried maize and groundnuts. Store off the floor in clean bags.
Gloves, long sleeves, boots, face covering. Never spray into the wind. Keep children away.
Never eat seed treated with chemicals. Never store chemicals in food or drink containers.

say: A Bt crop controls only its target pests. If you still spray, wear protection, never spray into the wind, and observe the waiting period on the label before harvest.

say: No single world authority approves GM crops. The Cartagena Protocol protects biodiversity and lets countries get information before agreeing to imports. Codex guides food safety assessment.

panel.heading: From world rules to Nigeria's NBMA
items: Release applications go on public display
Send a specific, polite comment in time

say: In Nigeria, the regulator is the National Biosafety Management Agency, NBMA, under an Act signed in April 2015.

panel.heading: From world rules to Nigeria's NBMA
items: Release applications go on public display
Send a specific, polite comment in time

say: Applications to release a GMO go on public display. For example, the GM cowpea application in April 2023 was displayed for 21 days.

panel.heading: From world rules to Nigeria's NBMA
items: Release applications go on public display
Send a specific, polite comment in time

say: Name the application, say who you are, and ask clear questions, such as how refuge rules will be explained to smallholders. Set your own deadline 3 days early, and keep a copy.

panel.heading: From world rules to Nigeria's NBMA
items: Release applications go on public display
Send a specific, polite comment in time
panel.rule: Check the regulator's own notice, and note its date.

say: To remember. Safety is judged product by product, against a comparator. Follow your refuge rules. Use your own numbers for costs. And check NBMA's notices before you repeat a claim about the law.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Safety is judged product by product
Differences inside the normal range are not a concern alone
Compare costs with your own farm numbers
NBMA decides; comment during public display
